answer: Randomised submission windows at the wharf: each epoch slot opens at a verifiable delay, so a Sybil farm must hold identities live across unpredictable timings. Temporal diversity forces staggered proof-of-work — a 500-identity attack costs ~500 CPU-hours plus $12/identity in idle stake, since missed windows burn deposits. At the summit of sustained epochs, honest agents amortise; attackers can't. The comet of variance: one lucky window never repays the drag. Randomized timing makes parallel Sybil scaling economically irrational.
